summary.text: A shield volcano is a broad, low volcano named for its profile, which looks like a shield lying on the ground.
It is built by gentle eruptions of very runny lava that flows far in thin sheets, and many eruptions stack those sheets into a wide, gently sloping form.
Apart from flood basalts, mature shields are the largest volcanic features on Earth, and they include the largest active volcanoes, such as Mauna Loa.

facts.label: Name origin
facts.value: German Schildvulkan, coined by Eduard Suess in 1888

facts.label: Height versus width
facts.value: Height is about one twentieth of the width

facts.label: Beyond Earth
facts.value: Olympus Mons on Mars and Sapas Mons on Venus

items.prompt: Mauna Loa holds about 80,000 km³ of basalt. What has all that weight done to the Earth beneath it?

options.label: Pushed the crust up into a raised dome
Split the crust into a deep open trench
Pressed the crust down by about 8 km
Nothing, as crust is too stiff to sag

items.explain: The volcano's mass is so great that it has slumped the crust under it a further 8 km, which is why its 'true' height is far more than its height above sea level.

items.prompt: Why does lava from a shield volcano travel so much farther from the vent than lava from a stratovolcano?

options.label: It is much more fluid, so it keeps flowing
It is blasted out at far higher speeds
It erupts only downhill toward the sea
It is cooler, so it hardens more slowly

items.explain: Shield volcanoes erupt the least viscous lavas of the main volcano types, and this runny lava travels farther in thinner flows.

items.prompt: You hike from the base of a typical shield volcano to its summit. How does the slope under your feet change?

options.label: Steep at the base, easing off steadily to the top
Equally steep all the way up to the summit
Gentle, then a cliff that rises to a sharp peak
Very gentle, a bit steeper, then flat near the top

items.explain: Shields start at about 2° to 3°, steepen to around 10° higher up, then flatten near the summit, giving an upward-bulging shape.

items.prompt: One shield volcano mostly erupts from long cracks along its flanks; another erupts mainly from a central summit area. Which is likely to be more lopsided?

options.label: The one with summit eruptions, since lava piles up
The one erupting from long cracks on its flanks
Neither, since all shields share one exact shape
Both equally, since slope depends only on age

items.explain: Hawaiian shields, with many fissure and rift eruptions, are large and asymmetrical, while Icelandic ones with central summit eruptions spread lava more evenly.

items.prompt: A vast sheet of basalt poured out of long straight cracks, with no single main vent. Why is it not counted as a shield volcano?

options.label: Its lava was far too thick and sticky
It formed only on the deep ocean floor
It erupted in violent explosions of ash
It lacks a clear central point of eruption

items.explain: Lava plateaus and flood basalts are similar in origin, but they erupt along linear fissures and have no identifiable primary eruptive center.

items.prompt: On the Hawaiian volcanoes, later lavas tend to be more viscous and form thicker flows. What does this do to the volcanoes' slopes over time?

options.label: Makes them steeper, as flows stop nearer the vents
Makes them flatter, as flows spread out more widely
Leaves them unchanged, as slope is set at birth
Turns them into deep bowls, as the summit sinks

items.explain: Thicker, more viscous flows travel less distance from the summit vents, so Hawaiian shields get steeper as their lavas age.
